subject: botany
question_text: Which is the largest botanical garden in the world? Name a few well known botanical gardens in India.

verification.note: Chapter 1 (The Living World) is sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Botany Fastrack, book p.3 (VSAQ 7 of 9), which prints the question and a model answer but no star ranks and no year citations. Only one source book is held for botany — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand is physics-only and no botany board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the board-paper back-test are both structurally impossible for this chapter; 'not checked' here means exactly that, never 'checked and clean'. The 1+1 mark split is a claim until a TS IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. BOOK GAP: the book lists the Indian gardens only as 'National botanical garden. Indian botanical garden.' with no places; the card writes the full standard names — Indian Botanical Garden, Howrah and National Botanical Research Institute, Lucknow.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Largest in the world

lines.text: Largest: Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, England

steps.why: One named garden answers the first half. The standard name is Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew — the book prints 'Royal botanical garden at Kew', a loose form of the same name.
common_mistakes: Writing only 'Kew garden' without the country. Add England so the answer is complete.
Naming the Indian Botanical Garden as the world's largest. Howrah is the famous Indian one; Kew is the largest.
steps.memory_tip: Count 1 + 2: one world's largest (Kew) and two Indian gardens (Howrah, Lucknow).
steps.margin_note: Name plus country in one line earns the mark.

steps.label: Gardens in India
lines: Well known botanical gardens in India:
steps.why: These are the two Indian gardens the NCERT chapter names. The book prints 'National botanical garden' and 'Indian botanical garden' without places — the full names with their cities are Indian Botanical Garden, Howrah and National Botanical Research Institute, Lucknow.
common_mistakes: Writing city names alone (Kolkata, Lucknow) without the garden names. Name the institution, then the city.
Mixing the two into one name, such as 'National Botanical Garden, Howrah'. Keep Howrah with the Indian Botanical Garden and Lucknow with NBRI.
steps.memory_tip: Pair each garden with its city: Indian — Howrah; National (NBRI) — Lucknow.
steps.margin_note: Two named Indian gardens are enough for 'a few'.

insider_note: This is pure recall — the marks are for the three institution names, so write them in full with their places.
